newsitem.title: UK: Russian debt rallies on news of debt accord by June.
newsitem.headline: Russian debt rallies on news of debt accord by June.

text.p: Russian debt rose sharply on Wednesday on news that the country planned to sign an agreement with the London Club of bank creditors to reschedule the debt of the former Soviet Union by June 30, market experts said.

"Russia has been quite topical with the minister saying the signing of the London Club will be in June," said one emerging market trader at a U.S. investment bank in London. Earlier today, Foreign Debt Department head Alexei Smirnov told Reuters in Moscow that Russia planned to sign the agreement by June and that it planned to reconcile the $20 billion necessary to close the deal.

Though the news boosted the price of Russian loans, some market experts said they were still a bit sceptical that the actual closing would occur by the end of June because of the complicated reconciliation process.

"We have seen quite a number of statements and what is still not clear is the extent to which the debt is reconciled. I think June looks a little aggressive because there has been slippage all the way down the line on this," said Philip Poole, director of research of emerging Europe and Russia at ING Barings.
"I think August looks feasible and that was their previous statement at the EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development). The issue remains reconciliation," Poole said.

Still, market experts said the actual closing of Russia's long-awaited debt rescheduling would be a positive for the market and would likely trigger a tightening of yield spreads against other emerging market debt instruments.

"I think it is actually a good time to be buying Russia in my view. If you look at Russia on a relative credit basis it looks very cheap," said Poole. "My feeling is that Russia should tighten relative to the rest of the market."
At 1330 GMT, Russian dollar denominated Vnesheconombank loans were 3/4 higher at 84-1/4 bid.

In the Latin Brady market, prices were mostly lower with Brazil giving back some of its sharp gains scored Tuesday on news that it kicked off Latin America's largest privatization by selling a controlling stake of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) for about $3.2 billion.
Brazilian "C" bonds were off 1/2 at 78-1/8 bid after rising as much as 1-1/8 to 78-5/8 on Tuesday.

"In a way there has been no followthrough buying in London today. It has been one of these buy on the rumour sell on the fact," said Peter West, director of emerging market research at West Merchant Bank in London.
While the CVRD deal was seen as a positive development for Brazil, market sources said there were still other concerns regarding the trade deficit and certain structural reforms.

"In the specific case of Brazil, this very positive development is to a certain extent being offset about concerns vis a vis the widening trade deficit and the apparent bogged down state fo the consititional reform process," West said.
West said there is a danger that many of the provisions of Brazil's public administrative reforms, which is currently being deliberated in the lower house of the Congress, will get watered down.
"We got one piece of very good news but there are ongoing concerns about other aspects of the Brazilian situation," West said.
